steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: 1944 Education Act: introduced the tripartite system - grammar schools (academic, 20% via 11+ exam), secondary moderns (practical/vocational, 75%), technical schools (few existed). Supposedly meritocratic but reproduced class inequality - middle-class children disproportionately passed the 11+.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: 1965: comprehensive education replaced the tripartite system. All pupils attend the same type of school regardless of ability. Aimed to reduce inequality and create social mixing. Evaluation: reduced the stigma of failing the 11+ but streaming within comprehensives reproduced inequality. Some areas retained grammar schools (the grammar school debate continues).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: 1988 Education Reform Act (Marketisation): introduced the National Curriculum, league tables, Ofsted inspections, and open enrollment (parents choose schools). Schools compete for pupils (like businesses). Smith and Noble: marketisation benefits middle-class parents who can work the system (house prices near good schools, knowledge of admissions). Whitty: creates a 'parentocracy' where educated, affluent parents have most choice.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Academies and free schools (2010 onwards): academies are state-funded but independent of local authority control; free schools are set up by parents, teachers or charities. Intended to raise standards through autonomy and innovation. Evaluation: some academies have improved results, but overall evidence is mixed. Critics argue they reduce democratic accountability and increase social segregation.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Describe how education policy has changed since 1944 and evaluate the impact of these changes. | Evaluate the impact of marketisation on educational inequality. | Assess whether comprehensive education has reduced inequality.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Tripartite (1944) = selection by 11+. Comprehensive (1965) = same school for all. Marketisation (1988) = competition and choice. Marketisation = PARENTOCRACY (educated parents have most choice). It BENEFITS the middle class and DISADVANTAGES the working class. Education policy has NOT significantly reduced class inequality because policies don't address structural disadvantage.
